intent: K6: make the gates see. Five checks report a number that is not the number, and every batch of this programme is refereed by them. components-01: the raw-control design-lint rule matches `<button` only when a character follows the tag name, so an opening tag that ENDS ITS LINE is invisible; the rule reports a handful and the tree holds over a hundred. app-04a: the try/catch census counts a route only when its catch calls serverErrorFromCatch, so eleven hand-rolled log-and-500 catches in six files are not counted and routesWithTryCatch reads 13 instead of 18. docs-02 and tooling-19: check-doc-links walks docs/ alone, so the 16 tracked markdown files outside it are unchecked, and C7's move broke three of their links. tooling-22: the line census walks src and tests alone, so scripts/ is unmeasured by the ratchet that referees every batch, including the census itself. tests-13: three exported test helpers have no caller, and the gate that would say so does not read tests/.

reasons.evidence: three closed-programme oracles are amended: c6 for the raw-control rule's zero check (components-01), c8 for routesWithTryCatch's target (app-04a), and c0 plus c8 for the census key set (tooling-22). Each amendment is for the one rule or key its ruled item fixes, and each is authored by a session that does not implement the fix.
five gates, three oracle amendments and two baselines, across tooling, tests and docs

programme: K6 of the refactor and clean-up programme, and the last of Phase 0. The plan filed this as K4 before the security set took that label. It is Phase 0 rather than Phase 3 because the recon and the plan that follow are both measured by these gates: a census that cannot see scripts/, or a lint rule that cannot see a raw control, would set the next plan's targets against numbers that are not true.
invariants: I1 EACH GATE IS PROVED BLIND BEFORE IT IS FIXED. For every one of the five, the oracle plants the violation the gate cannot see and requires the SHIPPED gate to stay green on it, then requires the fixed gate to go red. A fix with no proof of the blindness is a fix nobody can tell was needed.

I2 A NUMBER RISES BECAUSE THE GATE SEES MORE, NEVER BECAUSE THE TREE GOT WORSE. routesWithTryCatch 13 to 18 and the raw-control count are the same code counted properly. Each rise is held in a baseline with a written reason, and the reason says which gate changed.

I3 NO GATE IS LOOSENED. Every amendment narrows to the one rule or key its ruled item fixes, per Q-015. c6's other checks, c8's other measures and c0's other assertions are untouched, and no existing violation is blessed away.

I4 A DEFERRED GATE IS NAMED, NOT DROPPED. tooling-16, hooks-04, hooks-05 and critic-06 are blind gates this batch does NOT fix, each because the register gives it an unmet dependency. Each is listed in the notes with the batch it waits for.
I5 THE CLOSED ORACLES ARE AMENDED BY A SESSION THAT DOES NOT IMPLEMENT. Q-015, ruled 2026-09-12. Dated, attributed, and the reason in the same commit.
rollback: Each gate is a separate file and a separate baseline, so a revert can take one and leave the rest. The two that would need care are the ones with a closed-oracle amendment: reverting components-01 means reverting c6's amended assertion and the design-lint baseline together, and reverting app-04a or tooling-22 means reverting c8 (and c0 for tooling-22) with the census baseline. Nothing here changes product behaviour, migrates data or touches a route, so a revert restores the previous reported numbers and nothing else.
notes:
DEFERRED, with the dependency the register gives each one. tooling-16 (widen knip to tests/, test-harness/ and the root configs) carries `after: cross-cutting-22, tooling-02, POLICY-dependabot`, and its own fix line puts the harness orphans with tooling-02; widening knip before those land would turn the gate red on orphans this batch may not delete. hooks-04 (the raw-write rule blind to `fetch(` with a method) is to land after app-03's load move, and its fix includes converting sixteen writes to runWrite. hooks-05 (the census following an effect only through same-file functions) says in the register to hold its hits by name until hooks-01, hooks-09 and the chat read move land. critic-06 (the form-control name gate not knowing the house primitives) is to land with components-03, so the gate is green at merge. None of the four is dropped; each belongs to the batch that unblocks it, and the closing census reads them against this record.

STILL UNMEASURED, named here rather than left implied. scriptsLines counts scripts/ across the extensions the tooling is actually written in (.ts, .tsx, .mts, .cts, .css, .mjs, .cjs, .sh, .ps1, .py), which is 12,961 lines. It does NOT count the three mock servers (mock-hermes, mock-hindsight, mock-llm) or test-harness/, about a thousand lines between them, nor scripts/git-hooks/pre-push and a Dockerfile, which have no extension. The batch's intent field originally claimed the mock servers and the harness; the independent review caught that it did not deliver them, and the claim is withdrawn rather than the scope quietly widened. They are a follow-on for whichever batch measures the harness.

A RULING WORTH ASKING FOR. The review established something the record had wrong: hooks-04, hooks-05 and critic-06 are deferred here for a stronger reason than the dependency this record gives. None of the three has a ruled entry in the register at all, and Q-015 permits amending a closed oracle only for the one rule or key THE RULED ITEM fixes, so none of them could have amended c6 in this batch whatever their technical readiness. hooks-04 is the one worth putting back to the operator: the register at :3144 says its fix may land 'with a baseline and a c6 amendment (the same ruling as components-01)', and K6 already amends c6 and already opens a design-lint baseline, so the marginal cost of landing it here would have been small. It is not ducked; it is unruled.

review: Independent REVIEWER, clean context, verdict ACCEPT WITH FIXES, and all five are in the tree. It re-derived every widened number with its own instruments rather than reading the code, which is what caught the two findings that mattered. scriptsLines was 30 per cent short: the first cut counted the four extensions the APP is written in and silently left out 3,501 lines of shell, .mts, .cjs and Python under the very tree the measure is named for. In the batch whose thesis is that a gate must report a true number, that is the defect wearing the batch's own clothes. scripts/ now has its own extension set; src and tests keep the narrow one, because tests/ has its own .sh, .py and .cjs and widening globally would have moved testLines. A case name said the opposite of its assertion: 'the shared helper keeps the real read-only implementation', asserting that the helper keeps nothing. Renamed, and made comment-aware like its sibling three lines above. Also taken: a present-tense claim in read-only-actually-reads.test.ts that tests-13 makes false; the ANSWERS_500 character class tightened so it cannot run past the end of a statement; and three docstrings that overstated what their code does — the brace matcher folding a nested catch into its parent, the link gate now needing git and no longer seeing untracked markdown, and the route predicate counting only a catch that ALSO answers 500. Two of its observations are recorded rather than acted on. The c8 target at 18 is today's live reading, so the assertion is a tautology at merge and AT_C0/AT_C8 stay in the narrow measure's units; the ruling permitted either that or moving the key to the missed list. And the review corrected this record's own account of why three gates are deferred: see notes.
mutation: Twelve mutants against the committed tree, committed as tests/fixtures/mutants/T-0154.json. Most put a gate back the way the batch found it, because a batch that fixes gates is the one where a green suite proves least: the product did not change, so every product test passes either way. Two are the review's own findings turned into mutants. First run at d932cdad: 9 killed, 3 not. m11 came back INEFFECTIVE on the comment-only refusal, which is right in general and wrong for a mutant whose replacement prepends real code above a comment; it now carries force. m5 and m10 SURVIVED, and both were holes in the oracle rather than bad mutants, so they went to an ORACLE session under Q-015 rather than to the implementer. m5 is the one worth reading. The reviewer had already predicted the class — the oracle's differential re-implemented the same brace matching, so it could not cross-check it — but the precise tell only appeared when a real AST probe was built: the mutant moves routes.sites from 25 to 26 and does not move the file list at all, and the old differential compared only file lists. routes.sites was asserted nowhere in this repository. A green gate, an independent review and a mutation sweep each found a different layer of the same defect, and a fourth pass found what separated them. Re-run at d21c067c: 12 killed, 0 not.
deviation:
Five.

The record this batch opened with was wrong twice, and both were caught by the sessions it dispatched rather than by its author. The ORACLE session found that the c6 file is c6-the-page-layer.test.ts and not c6-the-page-layer-is-consistent.test.ts, which the claims and the record both named, and that there are 16 tracked markdown files outside docs/ and not 40. Both were corrected in the oracle's own commit.

The register prescribed something that does not exist. tests-13's fix line says to repoint read-only-is-testable.test.ts:99-102 'at the tests-01 factory'; tests-01 has no entry in the register, no plan reference, and no such factory is in tests/helpers. The assertion was restated instead of repointed: it required the shared helper to SPREAD the real api-auth module, and now requires it not to mock that module at all. That is strictly stronger — the old form passed a faithful spread and leaned on its sibling case to catch the unfaithful one — and it is true because the only thing that mocked api-auth was the dead helper this batch deleted. A mutant now holds it: m12 puts a faithful spread back.

The diff reached one file outside both lanes. read-only-actually-reads.test.ts states in the present tense that the shared helper mocks api-auth wholesale, which tests-13 falsifies; the reviewer found it outside the claims. Added to the lane and to this record rather than the edit defended.

The intent field overpromised. It said tooling-22 makes 'scripts/, the mock servers and the harness' measured; the ruled fix is a scriptsLines measure, and the mock servers and test-harness/ are still unmeasured. The claim is withdrawn and they are named as a follow-on in the notes, rather than the scope quietly widened to match the sentence.

The census baseline was re-cut five times across the batch, once because the measure now counts the tooling it is part of: editing a script moves scriptsLines, so the baseline has to be cut after the last edit to a script and not before. That is a property of the new measure rather than a mistake, and it is written here because the next batch to touch scripts/ will meet it.
